sources.notes: Road height is sampled from the existing approximately 64 m terrain raster and compressed to a 0.5 m interpolation tolerance relative to those samples; this is not road-surface survey accuracy. Station distances use the midpoint of corresponding border stations, not an official length measurement. This standing-start run begins at the first paired edge station and ends at the last; original timing metadata are retained. Finish speed is unconstrained, with no stopping zone modelled. Curbs and bend labels are geometry-based illustrations, not extracted from imagery or verified real curb locations; widths, heights and colours are assumed. Banking is unknown and assumed zero. Source border coordinates retain their separate feature-level licence; invalid cross-sections are interpolated. Imagery is an external display resource subject to provider terms; no image bytes are included.

measurement.note: Road-limit estimates from the pinned Environment Agency one-metre last-return laser-intensity raster captured 25–29 April 2019. This grayscale survey records reflected laser energy, not RGB photography. Driver-left and driver-right limits follow the visible narrow paved road, excluding hedges, farm aprons and adjoining field lanes. Most anchor gaps are approximately 36 m, with closer points through the field bends. Two right-side limits near stations 60 and 210 interpolate between neighbouring observations where vegetation or the side opening obscures the edge. The entrance endpoint follows the adjoining visible road lines and excludes the adjacent roof; the final endpoint follows the saved trace, not a surveyed timing or stopping line. Native raster pixels, vegetation and sparse interpolation limit accuracy. The original trace, timing and estimated terrain are retained; banking is unknown and rendered curbs illustrative.

borderInference.note: Road-border estimates reconstructed directly from complete, sparse image measurements on the existing trace cross-sections. All intervals interpolate between image anchors; they are not automatic detections or a continuous edge survey. Every saved edge station and anchor requires pinned-image coverage during authoring. Isolated missing pixels inside the road are not filled or used as boundary evidence. Imagery resolution is not survey accuracy. These borders have not been formally verified.
